newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt gives new privatisation target.
newsitem.headline: Egypt gives new privatisation target.

text.p: The minister in charge of Egypt's privatisation programme has said the state will sell shares in 51 public-sector companies during 1997 -- a lower target than the minister has given in previous statements.
Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid, quoted in the government newspaper al-Ahram on Saturday, said 40 of the 51 companies would be sold in full to large investors.
The state will sell shares in the other 11 companies by public subscription through the stock exchange, he added.
Obeid said in November that the state planned to sell some or most of the shares in 91 state companies by June 1998.
Earlier in the year he said the target for 1997 was three companies a fortnight throughout the year, making a total of 78.
Obeid has repeatedly announced ambitious privatisation targets which the government later failed to meet.
But the pace of sales did pick up in 1996, especially after May, when the government decided for the first time to relinquish control of a company through the stock exchange.
